title: Niccolo Sanpietro
summary: A Florentine Grand Financier who armed the Papacy.

claims.text: Sanpietro gave money and Swiss mercenary Enforcers to the Papal States, adding to the Swiss Guards; when Giulio de' Medici became Pope Clement VII, the Medici held sway over Church and banks alike.

title: Syndicate Enforcers (first edition)
summary: The Syndicate's strong arm in the criminal world.

claims.text: Enforcers run or assist crime syndicates, smugglers and street gangs in big cities, and trade in fear, punishing defaulters and guarding illicit markets.
Other Conventions see the Enforcers as a goon squad, which leads rivals to underrate the Syndicate's true size.

title: Outsourcing
summary: How the Syndicate collects gear from the other Conventions.

claims.text: Other Conventions owe the Syndicate favours, and Disbursements has them repay part of that debt in hardware: NWO limousines, Iteration X software and Progenitor drugs.
The flow runs both ways, with Syndicate lab creations sent to other Conventions' agents.

title: John Eaton Simcoe
summary: The Syndicate master of Diefenbakker's casino.

claims.text: In the 1950s Simcoe and other Syndicate members formed the Dominion Gaming Group, later DCG Ltd.
Simcoe runs the Diefenbakker's complex and sits on the Symposium that oversees Technocracy work in the Pacific Northwest, which in practice puts Simcoe in charge there.

title: Void Engineers and the Sons of Ether
summary: An old grudge over the Deep Universe.

claims.text: The first journeys into the Deep Universe began before the Etherites left the Technocracy, and their defection led to a small skirmish in space.
The two groups built the first craft for the Deep Universe together, then became fierce rivals; the Virtual Adepts' later departure stung the Void Engineers the same way.

title: Dark Side Base
summary: The Void Engineers' station on the Moon.

claims.text: The base relays and monitors the solar system and the Deep Universe posts, serves as the main laboratory Construct and training ground for the Border Corps.
A Moon-based team made the Convention's greatest find, Autochthonia, the ordered machine world where Iteration X's great computer is said to sit.

title: The Big Joke
summary: Why the other Conventions think the Void Engineers are harmless eccentrics.

claims.text: Elder Void Engineers keep up a long jest that makes the rest of the Union see them as space-show oddballs, which keeps the others from looking too closely.

title: Prime harvesting
summary: How Void Engineers collect and clean Nodes.

claims.text: Harvesting and sanitising Nodes is one of the Convention's main duties, and Quintessence and Tass power most Technocratic gear.
Most Universal Vessels carry Prime Absorption Devices; much of the research came from old Electrodyne Engineer records, though the word Ether is never spoken.
